channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: US employers defy economic shock from Iran war, add a surprisingly strong 115,000 jobs
item.description: The United States added 115,000 jobs in April, beating expectations, with the unemployment rate steady at 4.3 per cent. US employers defy economic shock from Iran war, add a surprisingly strong 115,000 jobs.

item.title: U.S. Fires on Iranian Tankers as Tehran Accuses Washington of ‘Reckless’ Attacks
item.description: The United States attacked Iranian targets after strikes on American ships, despite a proposed peace plan. The United States said it had attacked Iranian military targets in response to strikes on American ships.

item.title: US job growth beats expectations but consumer confidence at all-time low
item.description: The United States added 115,000 jobs in April, beating expectations, while the unemployment rate remained steady at 4.3 per cent. US job growth beats expectations but consumer confidence at all-time low.

item.title: US hopes for ‘serious offer’ from Iran today on latest proposal, despite exchange of strikes
item.description: US President Trump confirmed a ceasefire with Iran remains in place following an exchange of fire between the two countries. The situation escalated tensions, but Trump maintained that the ceasefire agreement holds.

item.title: US waiting on a response from Iran over proposals for ceasefire deal, says Rubio
item.description: US Senator Rubio says the US is waiting for Iran's response to proposals for a ceasefire deal. US waiting on a response from Iran over proposals for ceasefire deal, says Rubio The Guardian.

item.title: Tehran Accuses U.S. of 'Reckless' Attack in Strait as Trump Insists Cease-Fire Holds
item.description: Iran accused the US of a reckless attack in the Strait, despite Trump insisting a cease-fire holds. Iran Live Updates: Tehran Accuses U. S. of 'Reckless' Attack in Strait as Trump Insists Cease-Fire Holds The New York Times.

item.description: Analysts warn Putin acted with Xi's blessing, weakening global security. Putin acted with Xi’s blessing and weakened global security, analysts warn mezha. net.

item.title: Colombia's rogue hippos could find refuge in India
item.description: Colombia's invasive hippos may be relocated to India's wildlife reserve. In Colombia, a plan to cull Pablo Escobar's invasive hippos is challenged by an Indian billionaire's offer to relocate dozens of the animals to India's wildlife reserve instead.

item.title: How real is a coup threat against Russia's president?
item.description: Vladimir Putin has increased security and reduced public appearances. Increased security around Vladimir Putin and a scaling back of public appearances have given rise to suspicions of a coup or assassination attempt.

item.title: U.K. PM Starmer says he won’t step down after Labour’s losses
item.description: Keir Starmer refuses to step down after Labour's election losses. I’m not going to walk away and plunge the country into chaos, says Keir Starmer, as he acknowledged the results were ‘really tough’.

item.title: Reform UK makes election gains, humiliating Labour
item.description: Reform UK made gains in the election, defeating Labour. Keir Starmer's Labour has suffered a humiliating defeat as the hard right makes sweeping gains. Reform UK makes election gains, humiliating Labour.

item.title: US fires on and disables 2 more Iranian tankers as tensions rise in the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The US disabled two Iranian tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. US fires on and disables 2 more Iranian tankers as tensions rise in the Strait of Hormuz AP News.

item.title: Trump says ceasefire still in effect as Iran calls Strait of Hormuz attacks "point of no return"
item.description: US President Trump says a ceasefire remains in effect despite Iran calling the Strait of Hormuz attacks a "point of no return." Iran's statement suggests a fragile peace may be at risk.

item.title: South Africa’s top court revives impeachment inquiry against president
item.description: South Africa's top court has revived an impeachment inquiry against President Cyril Ramaphosa over a large sum of foreign currency stolen from his farmhouse in 2020. The scandal centres on a large sum of foreign currency stolen from President Cyril Ramaphosa’s farmhouse in 2020.

item.title: ‘Make up their own minds’: Pentagon releases first tranche of UFO files
item.description: The US Pentagon has released the first batch of UFO files, following a February order from President Trump. Critics argue the move is a distraction from more pressing issues. US President Trump ordered the release in February amid renewed public interest; critics claim distraction.

item.title: Four Men Found Guilty of Haiti President’s Assassination
item.description: Four men have been found guilty of assassinating Haitian President Jovenel Moïse in July 2021. Moïse's killing sparked a years-long wave of gang violence and chaos in Haiti. President Jovenel Moïse, 53, was gunned down in his bedroom in July 2021.

item.title: Virginia Supreme Court strikes down Democrats’ redistricting plan in US
item.description: Virginia's Supreme Court has blocked the state's Democrats from implementing a new redistricting plan, handing Republicans a key victory before the midterm elections. Virginia's top court blocks redistricting plan, handing Republicans a key win before crucial midterm elections.

item.title: Two Indian nationals onboard hantavirus-hit ship asymptomatic, under observation: Health Ministry
item.description: Two Indian nationals on a ship with hantavirus cases are asymptomatic and under observation. Eight probable cases of hantavirus infection have been reported onboard the vessel. According to WHO, the virus involved is the Andes strain of hantavirus, which is known to have limited capability of human-to-human transmission Three deaths have also been reported.

item.title: China Admits It Sent Experts To Pakistani Air Bases During Operation Sindoor
item.description: China sent experts to Pakistani air bases during Operation Sindoor, with 81 per cent of Pakistan's military hardware being Chinese. An overwhelming 81 per cent of Pakistan's military hardware is of Chinese origin.
